Petroleos de Venezuela SA Announces Major Investment to Boost Oil Output

Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA), Venezuela’s state-owned oil and gas producer, announced on Thursday a significant new investment initiative aimed at increasing the country’s crude oil production capacity over the next two years. The plan, which will see an estimated $2.5 billion injected into upstream operations, comes as the company seeks to revitalize its aging infrastructure and stabilize output in one of the world’s largest oil reserves.

The investment will focus primarily on modernizing key extraction facilities in the Orinoco Belt, widely regarded as Venezuela’s most prolific oil-producing region. According to PDVSA President Alejandro Martínez, the program will include upgrades to drilling equipment, enhanced maintenance of pipelines, and the deployment of new digital monitoring systems to improve operational efficiency. “This initiative marks a pivotal step for PDVSA as we work to restore our production capabilities and reaffirm Venezuela’s role as a reliable energy supplier,” Martínez said during a press conference in Caracas.

Industry analysts say the move is a positive signal for Venezuela’s oil sector, which has struggled with declining production rates in recent years. “The announced investment aligns with the government’s broader objective to attract capital and expertise into the sector,” noted Carolina Suárez, an energy analyst at Caracas-based research firm Consultora Energía. “With proper execution, these upgrades could help stem output declines and potentially lift daily production by up to 200,000 barrels by the end of 2025.”

The announcement has drawn support from the Oil Workers Union, which represents a significant portion of PDVSA’s workforce. “We welcome this commitment to strengthening our industry and preserving jobs,” said union leader Francisco Lugo. “Investment in technology and safety is critical for the future of our sector.”

The Venezuelan Ministry of Petroleum stated that the expansion project will also include environmental management measures, such as improved waste treatment and emissions monitoring. The ministry emphasized that sustainable practices would remain a priority as production ramps up.

PDVSA said it expects the first phase of the project to be completed by early 2025, with full implementation anticipated by late 2026.
